label: context.reference
text:
Lifecycle artifacts use system_lifecycle_events. lifecycle.event supports pre_tool_use, permission_request, post_tool_use, pre_compact, post_compact, session_start, session_end, user_prompt_submit, subagent_start, subagent_stop, stop and interrupt. session_end, subagent_start and interrupt are reactive; other events may be sync or async only as permitted by lifecycle_contract.json.

For a blocking continuation, the provider holds execution and authors a derived checkpoint. Its required_verified_artifacts names artifact_label lifecycle.decision, mark lifecycle.decision.allowed and verifier lifecycle_decision. Params pin the exact connection artifact/id, event id, emitter run, owner run, handler id, event, sync mode, handler type and subject artifact. Denied, blocked, stopped, malformed, replayed or mismatched decisions yield VerificationFailed with no mark.

Command handlers use granted Tool routes, MCP handlers exact World-interface operations, Prompt handlers exact provider inputs, and Agent handlers lifecycle.handler.task at an exact system_worker_* pin. The destination provider returns lifecycle.decision or lifecycle.handler.output. Async completion is correlated lifecycle.handler.output with no control effect.

The lifecycle.connection snapshot records source layer/path/trust and canonical destination-content SHA-256. Enabled untrusted or modified handlers are refused. Connect runs using the artifact binding, provider pin, grants, provider and handler checkpoints, and content-addressed run/policy evidence required by connection-authoring.schema.json. Installation alone connects nothing. Additional context and replacement refs in a decision must be authored on the continuation checkpoint; runtime does not infer or bind them.
